Thunder rolls from a cloudless sky, low and sustained, vibrating in the chest, coming from the direction of the distant peaks where no storm is visible and nothing moves.

A slow aurora descends lower than any natural light should reach, its crimson and gold curtains brushing the tops of the far hills like trailing silk dragged across the earth.

A slow tide of luminous pollen drifts from the ancient grove on the hill, catching the last daylight in drifting gold clouds that drift across the background like lazy smoke without heat or urgency.

The river in the valley below runs backward, visibly and impossibly, its current reversed against gravity up a gentle slope, its surface mirror-smooth while every tributary still flows normally around it.

Across the sky above the pass, bands of deep crimson and bruised violet have replaced the normal dusk, the colors too saturated and too still, holding long past the moment when they should have faded.
A slow spiral of ravens circles something far above the ruined keep on the distant hill, their gyre impossibly wide and impossibly patient, the birds at its center vanishing one by one into nothing.
Snow falls on the far side of the valley while the near side basks in dry late-summer warmth, the weather-line running sharp and straight as a ruled edge across the meadow below.
A rainbow hangs over the wetlands to the south but runs entirely in shades of deep gold and blood-red, its arc perfect, its colors wrong, its reflection doubled and sharp in the still water beneath.
